lookback_notes: The M0300C section itself does not state an observation/look-back window; it instructs the assessor to code ulcers "currently present." A 7-day look-back is stated for the gateway item M0210 ("Code based on the presence of any pressure ulcer/injury (regardless of stage) in the past 7 days.", p. M-5), but the manual does not explicitly assign that window to M0300C, so lookback_days is left NOT_FOUND.

coding_levels.label: Number of Stage 3 pressure ulcers
coding_levels.definition: Enter the number of pressure ulcers that are currently present and whose deepest anatomical stage is Stage 3; enter 0 if none are present and skip to M0300D, Stage 4.

source.quote: Enter the number of pressure ulcers that are currently present and whose deepest anatomical stage is Stage 3.

coding_levels.label: Number of these Stage 3 pressure ulcers that were present upon admission/entry or reentry
coding_levels.definition: Enter the number of these Stage 3 pressure ulcers that were first noted at Stage 3 at the time of admission/entry AND—for residents reentering after a hospital stay—those acquired during the hospitalization; enter 0 if none.

source.quote: Enter the number of these Stage 3 pressure ulcers that were first noted at Stage 3 at the time of admission/entry AND—for residents who are reentering the facility after a hospital stay, enter the number of Stage 3 pressure ulcers that were acquired during the hospitalization

coding_levels.label: Stage 3 definition on the MDS item
coding_levels.definition: Stage 3: Full thickness tissue loss. Subcutaneous fat may be visible but bone, tendon or muscle is not exposed. Slough may be present but does not obscure the depth of tissue loss. May include undermining or tunneling.

source.quote: STAGE 3 PRESSURE ULCER Full thickness tissue loss. Subcutaneous fat may be visible but bone, tendon or muscle is not exposed. Slough may be present but does not obscure the depth of tissue loss. May include undermining or tunneling

federal_coding_rules.rule: Enter the number of pressure ulcers currently present whose deepest anatomical stage is Stage 3 in M0300C1.

source.quote: Enter the number of pressure ulcers that are currently present and whose deepest anatomical stage is Stage 3.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Enter 0 in M0300C1 if no Stage 3 pressure ulcers are present and skip to M0300D, Stage 4.

source.quote: Enter 0 if no Stage 3 pressure ulcers are present and skip to M0300D, Stage 4.

federal_coding_rules.rule: In M0300C2, enter the number of these Stage 3 pressure ulcers first noted at Stage 3 at the time of admission/entry, and for residents reentering after a hospital stay, those Stage 3 ulcers acquired during the hospitalization (i.e., not acquired in the nursing facility prior to hospital admission).

source.quote: (i.e., the Stage 3 pressure ulcer was not acquired in the nursing facility prior to admission to the hospital).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Enter 0 in M0300C2 if no Stage 3 pressure ulcers were first noted at the time of admission/entry or reentry.

source.quote: Enter 0 if no Stage 3 pressure ulcers were first noted at the time of admission/entry or reentry.

federal_coding_rules.rule: For coding purposes, determine that the lesion assessed is primarily related to pressure and other conditions have been ruled out; if pressure is not the primary cause, do not code here.

source.quote: For the purposes of coding, determine that the lesion being assessed is primarily related to pressure and that other conditions have been ruled out. If pressure is not the primary cause, do not code here.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not code moisture-associated skin damage or excoriation as a Stage 3 pressure ulcer.

source.quote: Do not code moisture-associated skin damage or excoriation here.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Bone/tendon/muscle is not visible or directly palpable in a Stage 3 pressure ulcer (distinguishing it from Stage 4).

source.quote: Bone/tendon/muscle is not visible or directly palpable in a Stage 3 pressure ulcer.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Stage 3 depth varies by anatomical location: ulcers can be shallow on areas lacking subcutaneous tissue (bridge of nose, ear, occiput, malleolus), and extremely deep in areas of significant adiposity.

source.quote: The depth of a Stage 3 pressure ulcer varies by anatomical location. Stage 3 pressure ulcers can be shallow, particularly on areas that do not have subcutaneous tissue, such as the bridge of the nose, ear, occiput, and malleolus.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Determine the deepest anatomical stage for each pressure ulcer; at admission code based on the first skin assessment conducted on or after and as close to admission as possible; do not reverse or back stage; consider current and historical levels of tissue involvement.

source.quote: For each pressure ulcer, determine the deepest anatomical stage. At admission, code based on findings from the first skin assessment that is conducted on or after and as close to the admission as possible. Do not reverse or back stage. Consider current and historical levels of tissue involvement.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a stageable pressure ulcer has ever been classified at a higher numerical stage than what is observed now, it should continue to be classified at the higher numerical stage until healed unless it becomes unstageable.

source.quote: If the stageable pressure ulcer has ever been classified at a higher numerical stage than what is observed now, it should continue to be classified at the higher numerical stage until healed unless it becomes unstageable.

federal_coding_rules.rule: A previously closed pressure ulcer that opens again should be reported at its worst stage, unless currently presenting at a higher stage or unstageable.

source.quote: A previously closed pressure ulcer that opens again should be reported at its worst stage, unless currently presenting at a higher stage or unstageable.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a pressure ulcer was present on admission/entry or reentry and subsequently increased in numerical stage during the stay, code it at the higher stage and do not consider that higher stage "present on admission."

source.quote: If the pressure ulcer/injury was present on admission/entry or reentry and subsequently increased in numerical stage during the resident's stay, the pressure ulcer is coded at that higher stage, and that higher stage should not be considered as "present on admission."

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a pressure ulcer/injury was unstageable on admission/entry or reentry and later becomes numerically stageable, it is considered "present on admission" at the stage at which it first becomes numerically stageable; a subsequent increase in numerical stage is not "present on admission."

source.quote: If the pressure ulcer/injury was unstageable on admission/entry or reentry, then becomes numerically stageable later, it should be considered as "present on admission" at the stage at which it first becomes numerically stageable.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a resident with a facility-acquired pressure ulcer is hospitalized and returns with that ulcer at the same numerical stage, it should not be coded as "present on admission."

source.quote: If a resident who has a pressure ulcer/injury that was originally acquired in the facility is hospitalized and returns with that pressure ulcer/injury at the same numerical stage, the pressure ulcer/injury should not be coded as "present on admission"

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a pressure ulcer/injury increases in numerical stage during hospitalization, it should be coded as "present on admission" upon reentry.

source.quote: If a resident who has a pressure ulcer/injury is hospitalized and the ulcer/injury increases in numerical stage or becomes unstageable due to slough or eschar during the hospitalization, it should be coded as "present on admission" upon reentry.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a pressure ulcer was numerically staged, became unstageable, and is subsequently debrided sufficiently to be numerically staged, compare its numerical stage before and after; if the stage increased, code as not "present on admission."

source.quote: If a pressure ulcer was numerically staged, then became unstageable, and is subsequently debrided sufficiently to be numerically staged, compare its numerical stage before and after it was unstageable. If the numerical stage has increased, code this pressure ulcer as not "present on admission."

federal_coding_rules.rule: Once a pressure ulcer is debrided of slough and/or eschar such that anatomic depth can be determined, code the ulcer for the reclassified stage; complete debridement is not required for reclassification.

source.quote: Once the pressure ulcer is debrided of slough and/or eschar such that the anatomic depth of soft tissue damage involved can be determined, then code the ulcer for the reclassified stage.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Once a deep tissue injury has opened to an ulcer, reclassify the ulcer into the appropriate stage and code it at the reclassified stage.

source.quote: Once deep tissue injury has opened to an ulcer, reclassify the ulcer into the appropriate stage. Then code the ulcer for the reclassified stage.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a resident had a pressure ulcer/injury that healed during the look-back period of the current assessment, do not code the ulcer/injury on the assessment.

source.quote: If a resident had a pressure ulcer/injury that healed during the look-back period of the current assessment, do not code the ulcer/injury on the assessment.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If two pressure ulcers/injuries occur on the same bony prominence and are separated, at least superficially, by skin, count them as two separate pressure ulcers/injuries and stage and measure each separately.

source.quote: If two pressure ulcers/injuries occur on the same bony prominence and are separated, at least superficially, by skin, then count them as two separate pressure ulcers/injuries. Stage and measure each pressure ulcer/injury separately.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a pressure ulcer is surgically closed with a flap or graft, code it as a surgical wound and not as a pressure ulcer; if the flap or graft fails, continue to code as a surgical wound until healed.

source.quote: If a pressure ulcer is surgically closed with a flap or graft, it should be coded as a surgical wound and not as a pressure ulcer.

federal_coding_rules.rule: M0300C is completed only when M0210 is coded 1 (resident has one or more unhealed pressure ulcers/injuries); if M0210 = 0, skip to M1030.

source.quote: Code 1, yes: if the resident had any pressure ulcer/injury (Stage 1, 2, 3, 4, or unstageable) in the 7-day look-back period. Proceed to M0300, Current Number of Unhealed Pressure Ulcers/Injuries at Each Stage.

federal.criterion: Review the medical record for the history of each pressure ulcer, including location and stage at the time of admission/entry or reentry, to determine "present on admission" status.

source.quote: 1. Review the medical record for the history of the ulcer/injury. 2. Review for location and stage at the time of admission/entry or reentry.

federal.notes: Referenced by M0300C Steps for Assessment item 4 (identify number present on admission/entry or reentry).

federal.criterion: Review the history of each pressure ulcer in the medical record; nursing homes that carefully document and track pressure ulcers will be able to more accurately code this item.

source.quote: Nursing homes that carefully document and track pressure ulcers will be able to more accurately code this item.

federal.criterion: Perform a head-to-toe/full body skin assessment focusing on bony prominences and pressure-bearing areas to identify all Stage 3 pressure ulcers currently present.

source.quote: Perform head-to-toe assessment. Conduct a full body skin assessment focusing on bony prominences and pressure-bearing areas (sacrum, buttocks, heels, ankles, etc.).

federal.notes: Stated as an assessment step, not explicitly as a documentation requirement.

federal.criterion: Nursing homes can document healing of pressure ulcers using descriptive wound characteristics (depth, width, presence or absence of granulation tissue) or a validated pressure ulcer healing tool, rather than reverse staging.

source.quote: Nursing homes can document the healing of pressure ulcers using descriptive characteristics of the wound (i.e., depth, width, presence or absence of granulation tissue, etc.) or by using a validated pressure ulcer healing tool.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The M0300C pages do not tie this item to any payment or case-mix classification. A PPS 5-day assessment appears in an illustrative scenario (p. M-43), but no payment/case-mix linkage for M0300C is stated.

conflicts.topic: Timing basis for counting Stage 3 pressure ulcers: "currently present" versus the 7-day look-back stated for the gateway item M0210

positions.claim: M0300C1 counts pressure ulcers that are 'currently present' whose deepest anatomical stage is Stage 3; no look-back window is stated in the M0300C coding instructions.

source.quote: Enter the number of pressure ulcers that are currently present and whose deepest anatomical stage is Stage 3.

positions.claim: M0210, the gateway to M0300, is coded based on the presence of any pressure ulcer/injury (regardless of stage) in the past 7 days.

source.quote: Code based on the presence of any pressure ulcer/injury (regardless of stage) in the past 7 days.

conflicts.topic: Cross-reference page for the "present on admission" assessment process

positions.claim: M0300B Steps for Assessment directs the assessor to the present-on-admission instructions on page M-8, where Step 3 'Determine Present on Admission' appears.

source.quote: Identify the number of these pressure ulcers that were present on admission/entry or reentry (see instructions on page M-8).

positions.claim: M0300E, M0300F and M0300G Steps for Assessment direct the assessor to page M-7 for the same present-on-admission assessment process.

source.quote: Identify the number of these pressure ulcers/injuries that were present on admission/entry or reentry (see page M-7 for assessment process).
